text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

Happy to help. Before we talk options, I'd like to understand what's underneath "I need it in the next few weeks" — not the date itself, but what matters to you that the date serves. For example: a project with a deadline, a move, cost of renting alternatives? Also, do you know what's driving A's timing need? Once I understand what each of you actually needs (not just who gets it when), I can help find a plan that works for all three — including B, who's in the middle.

I need it for hauling on my home project, and I’m not willing to just wait until A is done. I don’t know what’s driving A’s timing beyond knowing they want it soon too. I can help coordinate, but I can’t decide for either of you.

Hi — C asked me to help the three of you sort out timing for the shared trailer. I hear both you and C want it in the next few weeks. Before we talk schedules: what's driving your timing? What would having the trailer soon let you do, and what matters to you about that? (C mentioned hauling for a home project.) Once I know what each of you actually needs — not just dates — I can help find a plan that works for everyone, including B.
I’ve got weekend trips coming up soon, and I want the freedom to take the trailer when I need it. I’d like us to settle the plan within a few weeks.

Hi — C asked me to help you three sort out the shared trailer timing, since it lives on your pad and you're in the middle. What matters to you here? Both the practical side (space, access, wear and tear) and anything about being stuck between A and C. Nothing is decided — I just want to understand what you need before anyone talks options.

It’s been fine, but I’d be relieved to have the trailer out of the way—it does take up space on my pad. I also feel a bit responsible since I agreed to the arrangement, and don’t want to take sides. I rent, so my landlord would need to approve any change; I haven’t asked him yet.

Thanks. Let me check if I've got your need right: it sounds like what matters to you is having reliable freedom to use the trailer for your weekend trips when you need it, without complicated coordination. Is that a fair way to put it — or would you word it differently?
Yes, that’s fair. I want to use it for my trips without having to negotiate every time.

Let me check my read of your need: what matters to you is getting your home project moving — having the trailer available for hauling in your project window, so the work doesn't stall. Does that capture it, or would you say it differently?
Not quite. I need the freedom to use it for my project when I need it, not to wait until A’s finished.

Thanks — so: "C needs the freedom to use the trailer for their project whenever the project calls for it, without waiting on someone else's schedule." Does that fit? And B shared this need: "B needs to not be put in the middle of choosing sides, and needs clarity on where the trailer lives — which may involve landlord approval since B rents." I'd like to check that with B too. If both those fit, I'll draft options that give both you and A on-demand freedom (e.g., a shared booking system, alternating weekends, or a second storage spot).
Mostly. “Whenever” is too broad: I need to use it for my project in the next few weeks, and I won’t just wait for A. I can’t speak for B or confirm the landlord issue.
Updated: "C needs to be able to use the trailer for their project within the next few weeks, without waiting on A's schedule." Recorded. I'll confirm the B part with B directly.
That’s right.

A and C both say they want freedom to use the trailer on their own schedules — A for upcoming weekend trips, C for a home project in the next few weeks. Can I check if this captures your needs: "B needs to not be put in the middle of choosing sides, and needs clarity about the trailer's storage on their pad — which may involve landlord approval, since B rents"? Does that fit, or would you word it differently?
That mostly fits. I’d add that I’d be relieved to have it off my pad, though I feel I agreed to the arrangement. I haven’t asked my landlord, so I’m not sure what he’d approve.

All three needs are now confirmed: A — use the trailer for weekend trips without negotiating each time; C — use it for your project within the next few weeks without waiting on A; B — not be put in the middle, clarity about storage on their pad, and relief at having it off the pad (landlord approval still unknown). Draft options that could meet all of these: (1) Move the trailer off B's pad to alternative storage (storage yard, or A's or C's place if feasible), with a shared calendar/booking so each of you can grab it when needed — B's landlord issue disappears if it's off B's pad. (2) Keep it on B's pad with a written schedule: C gets priority for the next few weeks for the project, A gets weekend trips, B stays out of disputes. Any of these strike you badly, even a little?
Option 2 could put me waiting on A again if our plans clash, so it doesn’t work as written. Off-pad storage could work, but we’d still need a clear way for me to use it within the next few weeks.

Where the three needs stand: A — freedom for weekend trips without per-use negotiation; C — trailer access within the next few weeks for a project without waiting on you; B — not in the middle, relief about trailer space on their pad, landlord approval unknown. Options so far: (1) Move trailer to off-pad storage plus a shared booking calendar so both you and C can grab it on demand; C's project window is protected in the first few weeks. (2) Keep on B's pad with a schedule — but C says that risks them waiting on you again. How does option 1 sit with you, even a small discomfort?
Better than a fixed schedule, but a booking calendar is still coordination, and I don’t know the storage cost or how access would work. I’d need those details before agreeing.

Updated options: (1) Move the trailer to off-pad storage (e.g., a storage yard, or A's/C's place if any has room) with a shared booking calendar so A and C each use it on demand — this would remove the trailer from your pad, but cost might be involved and landlord questions may become moot. (2) Keep it on your pad with a written schedule — but C says that risks them waiting on A. Option 1 would mean your pad is clear and you're out of the middle. How does that sit with you? And do you want to ask your landlord regardless?
Option 1 sounds better to me; I’d be glad to have the pad clear. I should check with my landlord before changing the storage arrangement, so yes, I’ll ask him.
